pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is a role of trees and plants? (1 mark)
   A. They give oxygen and shade
   B. They stop rain forever
   C. They dry up rivers
   D. They make the sun set

2. Which plant is the holy basil? (1 mark)
   A. Beri
   B. Tulsi
   C. Peepal
   D. Sal

3. What should we never throw into rivers? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic and waste
   B. Clean leaves
   C. Rainwater
   D. Rain

4. Which Jain teacher is linked with the bank of the Rijubalika river? (1 mark)
   A. Prahlad
   B. Valmiki
   C. Lord Mahavir
   D. Guru Nanak

5. The soil in a shamba belongs to which element? (1 mark)
   A. Vayu
   B. Akash
   C. Agni
   D. Prithvi

6. How can water be used in worship? (1 mark)
   A. To wash the hands and feet before prayer
   B. To burn incense
   C. To build the temple roof
   D. To make bells ring

7. In which city was Parshvanath born? (1 mark)
   A. Nairobi
   B. Lumbini
   C. Lahore
   D. Varanasi

8. What is a Tirthankar in Jainism? (1 mark)
   A. A king
   B. A festival
   C. A teacher who shows the path across the river of life
   D. A temple

9. Who was Prahlad? (1 mark)
   A. The young son of Hiranyakashipu who loved Vishnu
   B. A river
   C. A Jain monk
   D. A Sikh Guru

10. What does Asteya mean? (1 mark)
   A. Sing every day
   B. Fast all day
   C. Sit still
   D. Do not take what is not given

11. Which Tirthankar is the twenty-third of Jainism? (1 mark)
   A. Mahavir
   B. Parshvanath
   C. Buddha
   D. Guru Nanak

12. Sri Guru Ram Das Ji was which Guru of the Sikhs? (1 mark)
   A. The third
   B. The fourth
   C. The first
   D. The tenth

13. Whom did Ram marry in the Bal Kaand? (1 mark)
   A. Saraswati
   B. Ganga
   C. Kaikeyi
   D. Sita

14. What is the holy scripture of the Sikhs? (1 mark)
   A. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji
   B. Kalpasutra
   C. Ramayan
   D. Dhammapada

15. In which script is Guru Granth Sahib Ji written? (1 mark)
   A. Arabic
   B. Swahili script
   C. Roman
   D. Gurmukhi

16. Who took Ram and Lakshman to protect his forest prayers? (1 mark)
   A. Sage Valmiki
   B. King Shibi
   C. Sage Vishwamitra
   D. Guru Nanak

17. Who was Sigala? (1 mark)
   A. A Sikh Guru
   B. A king of Ayodhya
   C. A young man taught by the Buddha
   D. A Jain monk

18. What do Sikhs eat together in the gurdwara? (1 mark)
   A. Langar, the community meal
   B. Fasting food
   C. Nothing
   D. Prasad only from a priest

19. What is the lesson of Bharat refusing the throne? (1 mark)
   A. Never obey
   B. Be humble and do not be greedy for power
   C. Grab wealth
   D. Take what you like

20. Who gave the Sigalovada Sutta talk? (1 mark)
   A. Guru Arjan Dev
   B. The Buddha
   C. Mahavir
   D. Valmiki

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain why the time and place of the defeat of Hiranyakashipu are special in the story. (3 marks)

22. Name the two Buddhist scriptures in this lesson. (2 marks)

23. Explain the meaning of Ahimsa and give two ways to practise it. (3 marks)

24. Describe the lessons of the Uttaradhyayan Sutra. (4 marks)

25. Who compiled Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji first, and who declared it the eternal Guru? (2 marks)

26. Describe how the Bodhi tree is linked with the Buddha. (3 marks)

27. State two reasons why trees and plants are important. (2 marks)

28. Explain what Hindus mean by an Avtar. (2 marks)

29. Why should we not bully others, according to the teachings in this lesson? (2 marks)

30. Why should we not pollute rivers? (2 marks)

31. Discuss how people of different faiths show respect for water and trees. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — They give oxygen and shade
   Plants clean the air and give shade.

2. B — Tulsi
   Tulsi is the holy basil plant.

3. A — Plastic and waste
   Waste harms water and living things.

4. C — Lord Mahavir
   Lord Mahavir is believed to have become fully enlightened there.

5. D — Prithvi
   Soil is earth, or Prithvi.

6. A — To wash the hands and feet before prayer
   Washing before prayer is a way of showing cleanliness and respect.

7. D — Varanasi
   Parshvanath was born as a prince in Varanasi.

8. C — A teacher who shows the path across the river of life
   Tirthankars guide people to freedom.

9. A — The young son of Hiranyakashipu who loved Vishnu
   Prahlad stayed faithful to Vishnu.

10. D — Do not take what is not given
   Asteya means not stealing.

11. B — Parshvanath
   Parshvanath is the twenty-third Tirthankar.

12. B — The fourth
   He came after Guru Amar Das Ji.

13. D — Sita
   Ram married Sita in Mithila.

14. A — Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji
   Sikhs follow it as their eternal Guru.

15. D — Gurmukhi
   It is written in Gurmukhi.

16. C — Sage Vishwamitra
   Vishwamitra asked for their help.

17. C — A young man taught by the Buddha
   The talk was given to him.

18. A — Langar, the community meal
   Everyone eats together in the langar.

19. B — Be humble and do not be greedy for power
   He knew the throne belonged to Ram.

20. B — The Buddha
   The Buddha spoke to a young man named Sigala.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Narsimha was neither man nor animal, it was neither day nor night, and it happened at the doorway, neither inside nor outside, so the king's gift did not protect him.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three details.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Dhammapada and the Sigalovada Sutta.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ahimsa is not harming any living being by thought, word or action. We practise it by not bullying and by caring for animals and plants.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for each example.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Practise Ahimsa, be honest, control greed and anger, and respect teachers (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: Guru Arjan Dev Ji compiled it; Guru Gobind Singh Ji declared it the Guru.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each name.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Prince Siddhartha sat under a Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya and became the Buddha, the Awakened One. Buddhists honour the tree because of this.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the tree, 1 mark for Siddhartha, 1 mark for enlightenment or Bodh Gaya.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: They give oxygen, shade, food and medicine; their leaves are used in worship (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: A form in which God is believed to come to earth to protect goodness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for God coming to earth and 1 mark for protecting goodness.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Enlightened Beings teach kindness and Ahimsa, so we should not harm others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for kindness or Ahimsa, 1 mark for a link to bullying.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Polluted rivers harm plants, animals and people who use the water, and take away the sacredness of the water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

31. (5 marks)
   Answer: Hindus honour the Ganga and Tulsi; Sikhs remember the Beas and the Ber tree; Jains honour the Rijubalika and the Sal tree; Buddhists honour the Bodhi tree. All value water and trees and take care of them.
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for each faith correctly described, up to 4 marks, and 1 mark for the idea that all faiths show respect.
